_meta.indication: BRIVIACT is indicated as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled, randomized, fixed-dose
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥16 to 70 years with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 7-day (per week) partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Percent reduction over placebo: 50 mg/day 9.5% and 100 mg/day 17.0% (neither marked statistically significant in the label table)

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled, randomized, fixed-dose
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥16 to 70 years with refractory partial-onset seizures
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 7-day partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.n: 396 (PBO=98, 20 mg/day=100, 50 mg/day=101; the efficacy table also included a 5 mg/day arm, N=96)
pivotal_trials.result: 50 mg/day produced a statistically significant reduction over placebo; the label-reported adjusted mean percent reduction was 16.9% (marked statistically significant), and the primary analysis showed a 12.8% (95% CI 1.7, 22.6) reduction, p=0.025

nct_ctgov.title: Double-blind, Randomized Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of Brivaracetam in Adults With Partial Onset Seizures

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, multinational, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled, randomized, fixed-dose (concomitant levetiracetam excluded)
pivotal_trials.population: Patients aged ≥16 to 80 years with refractory partial-onset seizures; concomitant levetiracetam excluded
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent reduction in 28-day partial-onset seizure frequency over placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant reductions over placebo: label-reported adjusted mean percent reductions of 25.2% (100 mg/day) and 25.7% (200 mg/day); primary-analysis percent reductions were 22.8% (95% CI 13.3, 31.2) and 23.2% (95% CI 13.8, 31.6), both p<.001

nct_ctgov.title: Brivaracetam Efficacy and Safety Study in Subjects With Partial Onset Seizures

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (BRIVIACT N=803 vs placebo N=459) were somnolence and sedation (16% vs 8%), dizziness (12% vs 7%), fatigue (9% vs 4%), and nausea/vomiting (5% vs 3%). Warnings include suicidal behavior/ideation, neurological adverse reactions (somnolence, fatigue, dizziness, and gait disturbance), psychiatric adverse reactions, and hypersensitivity (bronchospasm and angioedema).
target_moa: The precise mechanism of anticonvulsant activity is not known; brivaracetam displays a high and selective affinity for synaptic vesicle protein 2A (SV2A) in the brain, which may contribute to the anticonvulsant effect.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is acceptable and the clinical trial design is similar to previously approved products in the class.

description.text: Added use as monotherapy for treatment of partial onset seizures in patients 16 years and older

citations.quote: These Prior Approval supplemental new drug applications provide for the use of BRIVIACT (brivaracetam) as monotherapy for the treatment of partial onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.

basis.text: The application was a Standard (not Priority) review.

citations.quote:
Application Number(s)	NDA 205836, NDA 205837, NDA 205838
Priority or Standard	Standard

summary.text: Brivaracetam (BRIVIACT) was a new molecular entity approved in a standard-review, first-cycle NDA for adjunctive therapy of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years and older, supported by three adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 studies (N01252, N01253, N01358); it carried no accelerated approval or special designations, and pediatric studies were required as postmarketing requirements.

citations.quote: It is a new molecular entity intended to be used as adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial-onset seizures in patients 16 years of age and older with epilepsy.
This conclusion is supported by evidence from three adequate and well-controlled studies (studies 1252, 1253, and 1358) that evaluated the use of brivaracetam at various doses.
Your deferred pediatric studies required under section 505B(a) of the FDCA are required postmarketing studies.

requirement.text: 3042-1: A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure similar to the exposure effective in adults with partial onset seizures.

citations.quote: 3042-1 A pharmacokinetic analysis to determine a dosing regimen in children from 4 years to less than 16 years of age that provides drug exposure that is similar to the exposure that is effective in adult patients with partial onset seizures. This analysis will require pharmacokinetic data from studies of both adult and pediatric patients. These studies have already been performed.

requirement.text: 3042-2: A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether bioavailability of the IV and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the IV formulation.

citations.quote: 3042-2 A pharmacokinetic and safety analysis in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age to determine whether the bioavailability of the intravenous and oral formulations is similar and to determine an acceptable safety margin of the intravenous formulation when administered at doses that are found acceptable for oral administration.

requirement.text: 3042-3: A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age.

citations.quote: 3042-3 A prospective, randomized, controlled, double-blinded, efficacy and safety study of brivaracetam for the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 4 years of age. requirement.text: 3042-4: Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age; at least 200 patients must be enrolled.

citations.quote: 3042-4 Long-term safety study of brivaracetam in the adjunctive treatment of partial onset seizures in children from 1 month to less than 16 years of age. Routine safety measures should be monitored. Behavioral and cognitive endpoints should be included. A total of at least 200 patients must be enrolled. Subjects should be balanced among age cohorts.
